headline: Ocean Cleanup Removes 463,000 Pounds of Trash in Single Catch
meta_description: The Ocean Cleanup intercepted 463,000 pounds of waste using a river barrier in Guatemala, preventing trash from reaching the Caribbean Sea.
summary_short: A river barrier in Guatemala stopped hundreds of thousands of pounds of trash before it could pollute the Gulf of Honduras and Caribbean waters.
body:
The Ocean Cleanup successfully stopped 463,000 pounds of trash from reaching the Gulf of Honduras in a single catch, using an innovative river barrier system in Guatemala to intercept waste before it flows into the Caribbean Sea.

The operation demonstrates how targeted intervention at the source can prevent ocean pollution on a massive scale. By placing the barrier in a river—rather than attempting cleanup in open water—The Ocean Cleanup addressed the problem upstream, where plastic and debris naturally concentrate as they travel downstream toward the coast.
quick_facts: 463,000 pounds of trash intercepted in one catch
River barrier system located in Guatemala
Waste prevented from reaching the Gulf of Honduras
Cleanup occurs before trash enters the Caribbean Sea
